question: Does the frozen curvature model improve one-sided continuation on genuinely unused compatible precursor-ink units, and does an independently fitted calibration layer achieve its declared coverage target?

frozen_reference_model.candidate: fixed two-contrast shared Gaussian correction with full reference residual
frozen_reference_model.changes_allowed_before_confirmation: None unless a separately versioned new candidate and protocol are created.

data_role_rule: Reserve real calibration and confirmation units before inspecting their target responses; do not split masks or related runs from one physical unit across roles. No consumed25P/46external targets are newly independent.
target_rule: Only native declared positions strictly above the highest observed anchor and within frozen global support; no interpolation or generated targets as measured truth.

primary_endpoint.suggestion: Per-unit CRPS on log viscosity averaged over continuation targets with normalized trapezoidal log-rate weights, then aggregated by the declared independent unit.
primary_endpoint.historical_endpoint_note: This is a possible new endpoint; it does not replace the original native-position three-layout endpoint.

secondary_endpoints: log RMSE or pooled MSE with stated weights
marginal coverage at the fixed nominal level
all prediction failures, including zero-coverage units
freeze_and_reveal: 1. Author signs material/unit/metadata/admission plan and complete fields, then records actualUTC and input/runtime hashes.
2. Fit no correction on confirmation outcomes; freeze any calibrator using only its reserved units and record its new version.
3. Read only six allowed anchors per confirmation unit and freeze all candidate/control predictions with source hashes.
4. A steward reveals complete original targets once; score all eligible units with registered weights and explicit failures.
5. Report the full cohort and all controls, whether successful or not; no posthoc reclassification as independent after revision.

calibration_extension.method: curve-level split conformal band around frozen log-Gaussian predictor
calibration_extension.formula: s_i=max_{j in H_i}|y_ij-mu_ij|/sigma_ij; k=ceil((n_cal+1)(1-alpha)); q=s_(k) if k<=n_cal, otherwise +infinity; B_j=[mu_j-q*sigma_j,mu_j+q*sigma_j].
calibration_extension.score_scale: dimensionless natural-log viscosity; sigma_ij must be positive under a fixed pre-calibration rule
calibration_extension.exchangeability: Conditional on model training and frozen score/design, reserved calibration units and the future unit must be exchangeable as complete units. Related coordinates or runs are not separate units. If the scientific target is a new batch, use a defensible batch-level score/design.
calibration_extension.guarantee_if_assumptions_hold: Marginal probability over the calibration sample and a new compatible unit of all declared finite-grid targets lying in their bands is at least1-alpha. Not conditional per chemistry/subgroup and not coverage between grid points.
calibration_extension.small_sample_rule: If k>n_cal, use an infinite band rather than silently lowering the order-statistic index. No usable finite-band or power guarantee is implied by a proposed sample count.
calibration_extension.density_warning: Conformal bands are prediction sets, not a calibrated joint density or generative law. Do not assign them a newly inventedCRPS/joint log density; keep the original Gaussian law distinct.
calibration_extension.unit_log_to_viscosity: Multiply exp(band endpoints) by eta_ref=1Pa s.
calibration_extension.proof_note: A scalar maximum score makes finite-grid simultaneous inclusion equivalent to s_new<=q. Exchangeability supplies the rank bound; no independence of coordinates within a curve is assumed.

prohibition: Do not fill sample sizes, tolerance, batch identities or registration times from old scores or invented values. This template is not an executed or preregistered study.
